// P3 upper landing: a two-by-four hall at the stair top. Its floor is the lane to three doors (master bedroom x42 z10,
// back bedroom x42 z13 and the x43 z14 opening) and to the tower ladder at (44, 8..12, 9), so every floor cell stays
// clear. The only furniture is wall-hung at y10..11: a birch top-slab shelf with a flower pot on the west wall (the focal
// piece, where the stair comes up), and one hanging lantern under the ceiling at (43, 11, 10) that lights all six cells.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  const legend = {
    "L": ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
    "S": ["birch_slab", { type: "top" }],
    "P": "flower_pot",
  };
  // origin [43, 8, 10]: x 43..44 within a row, z 10..13 down the rows; y 8 and 9 stay empty (the lane and headroom)
  // one layer per y (y 8..11), each layer its rows z 10..13
  const empty = ["..", "..", "..", ".."];
  layers(g, [43, 8, 10], legend, [
    empty,
    empty,
    ["..", "..", "S.", ".."],
    ["L.", "..", "P.", ".."],
  ]);
}

input.summary:
parts/room-23.mjs (P3 upper landing) now builds with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. The birch shelf and flower pot moved from the west side (x43 z12, blocked by the roof's underside) to the east wall at (44,10,10) and (44,11,10). make.sh writes build.nbt and this part reports "3 placed; refused 0; offPalette []".</summary>
<parameter name="finished">true
left: make.sh's whole-build output still shows REFUSED writes in other parts (Roofs 91, P4 porch, P4 wing kitchen, P4 attic bedroom, P5 barn aisle and loft). Those are outside this task and were not touched.
The room was not re-walked or lit-checked after the move. The shelf and pot are on the east side at y10..11, above the walking layer, so the floor should be unchanged, but `mcd room` was not run.

waste.what: Found which earlier part owned the refused cells by dumping every block in x42..45 y7..12 z9..14 through a throwaway probe script, then checked the candidate cells one at a time.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one probe script of about 40 lines; output was over 100 lines of block dump to read by eye
waste.tool: `mcd plan` marks only the floor layer, so it showed the roof's underside as free floor. A layers() dry run, or `mcd plan --y 10,11` marking cells already occupied by earlier parts ('o' at every layer), would have shown the blocked cells before the first make.sh.

waste.what: Chose a new shelf spot by hand: tested which wall cells were solid and which of (44,10,10) and (44,11,10) were air, and worked out the layers() rows for the new spot.
waste.cost: 2 probe queries and one edit of two layer rows plus the comment; 2 make.sh runs
waste.tool: a `mcd place-check` or layers() option that takes a candidate cell list and returns the first free cell per wall that has solid backing, so the designer picks from valid spots instead of retrying.
